scope: Claim-level mathematical dependencies in the reviewed LaBRADOR literature.

discovery.caveat: 目录时点与范围不同，不相加；99是候选文件不是论文数；不声称穷尽所有引用。

source_policy: One-based physical PDF pages unless a printed page is also stated. Local versions are fixed by SHA-256; official metadata was checked separately.

papers.title: LaBRADOR: Compact Proofs for R1CS from Module-SIS
papers.anchors: PDF pp10、30–31；既有研究 notes/jl_audit.md 与 CLOSEOUT.md
papers.affected_claim: 研究起点：严格 2^-128 JL 数值预算未成立，其他关系与提取接口缺项见既有研究归档。
papers.limits: 原文部分使用近似符号；现有局部反例不等于否定所有近似写法、完整总误差预算或实现安全。原论文单列，不混入下游计数。

papers.title: RoKoko: Lattice-based Succinct Arguments, a Committed Refinement
papers.affected_claim: Lemma 5 repeats the exact 256-row, sqrt(30) lower-tail budget; Lemmas 6–7 use it in structured projection.
papers.limits: Independent commitments and sumcheck claims have their own proof obligations.

papers.title: Orthus: Practical Sublinear Batch-Verification of Lattice Relations from Standard Assumptions
papers.affected_claim: Theorem 5 repeats the strict lower-tail bound; Theorems 3–4 use its failure budget.
papers.limits: The revised compressed configuration uses a separate infinity-norm theorem with threshold 0.49.

papers.title: Grand Danois: Succinct Multilinear Polynomial Commitments over Lattices
papers.affected_claim: Lemma 2.5 uses the same numerical lower-tail premise, introduced explicitly as heuristic; later projection proofs use it.
papers.limits: The existing strict lower-tail certificate also covers this lemma’s norm-relative event.

papers.title: Aggregating Falcon Signatures with LaBRADOR
papers.affected_claim: The heuristic JL lemma sets C2=30 at lambda=128; the later failure-density analysis uses a 2^-lambda term.
papers.limits: The numerical instantiation needs recalibration; the general predicate-special-soundness framework is a separate contribution.

papers.title: Symphony: Scalable SNARKs in the Random Oracle Model from Lattice-Based High-Arity Folding
papers.affected_claim: Lemma 2.2 imports the approximate JL constants used by the range-proof slack and extraction analysis.
papers.limits: The paper uses approximate inequalities. Its generic compiler remains a conditional result.

papers.title: A Toolkit for Succinct Lattice-Based Zero Knowledge Proofs
papers.affected_claim: The terminal uses sqrt(128/30), 256-row Bin1 projections and the original LaBRADOR composition theorem.
papers.limits: The November revision also includes a distinct infinity-norm result and changes to LNP-Lite.

papers.title: Lemur+: Compact Post-Quantum Synchronized Multi-Signatures and Multi-Hop Aggregation
papers.affected_claim: The extracted-norm and MSIS estimates use delta_LB=sqrt(128/30); opening soundness relies on the selected backend.
papers.limits: The generic HVC-SOP/KOTS construction is stated separately from this instantiation.

papers.title: Greyhound: Fast Polynomial Commitments from Lattices
papers.affected_claim: The succinct evaluation proof delegates its final short relation to LaBRADOR.
papers.limits: The C implementation uses Rademacher projection entries. The ternary mathematical example requires a separate implementation-level analysis.

papers.title: Hachi: Efficient Lattice-Based Multilinear Polynomial Commitments over Extension Fields
papers.affected_claim: The 55.1KB composition estimate includes a Greyhound tail, which in turn invokes LaBRADOR.
papers.limits: The Rust prototype measures the first Hachi round; ring switching and sumcheck are independently described.

papers.title: The LaZer Library: Lattice-Based Zero Knowledge and Succinct Proofs for Quantum-Safe Privacy
papers.affected_claim: The succinct-proof branch uses the LaBRADOR implementation and its parameter assumptions.
papers.limits: LaZer also exposes a separate linear-size proof branch.

papers.title: Unmasking TRaccoon: A Lattice-Based Threshold Signature with An Efficient Identifiable Abort Protocol
papers.affected_claim: The LaBRADOR-based ZK composition imports failure-density and knowledge-error premises from the Falcon analysis.
papers.limits: Its binary-projection lemma uses a different distribution and constants; the underlying TRaccoon signature is a separate layer.

papers.title: LaBinius – Fast Lattice-Based Binary Polynomial Commitment Scheme
papers.affected_claim: Recursive opening links a vendored LaBRADOR backend; Theorem 2 explicitly includes kappa_Lab.
papers.limits: The nonrecursive PCS and binary-field arithmetic have separate analysis and measurements.

papers.title: RoK, Paper, SISsors – Toolkit for Lattice-based Succinct Arguments
papers.affected_claim: An optional LaBRADOR second compression underlies the roughly 100KB estimate.
papers.limits: The main subtractive-set/vSIS protocol has its own proof chain.

papers.title: LatticeFold: A Lattice-based Folding Scheme and its Applications to Succinct Proof Systems
papers.affected_claim: LaBRADOR is one possible final compressor for the IVC proof.
papers.limits: The paper also offers a Stark terminal and uses sumcheck for its core range checks.

papers.title: Serval: Slack-Free l2-Sound Polynomial Commitments from Lattices
papers.affected_claim: The optional compressed construction includes epsilon_La in its error expression.
papers.limits: The measured prototype implements the baseline. LaBRADOR compression is an analytical extension in the reviewed version.

papers.title: Succinct Shortness Check Under a Few Kilobytes via Tensor Train Random Projections
papers.affected_claim: The comparison table and host-integration examples use the older JL calibration.
papers.limits: TTRP replaces the old projection with its own probability and composition results.

papers.title: Non-Malleable Reductions of Knowledge
papers.affected_claim: The zk-LaBRADot case study uses separate heuristic premises.
papers.limits: Bin2, 512 rows and sqrt(26) differ from the audited event; a transfer of the existing counterexample remains unestablished.

papers.title: RoK and Roll – Verifier-Efficient Random Projection for O-tilde(lambda)-size Lattice Arguments
papers.affected_claim: Independent direct projection bounds and a final explicit witness.
papers.limits: The concrete parameters use the paper’s own Lemmas 4–5.

papers.title: SALSAA: Sumcheck-Aided Lattice-based Succinct Arguments and Applications
papers.affected_claim: Projection guarantees follow RoK and Roll; the terminal sends the remaining witness.
papers.limits: The dependency direction runs from SALSAA to later RoKoko work, rather than importing RoKoko’s numerical lemma into SALSAA.

papers.title: LatticeFold+: Faster, Simpler, Shorter Lattice-Based Folding for Succinct Proof Systems
papers.affected_claim: LaBRADOR appears in related work and performance comparisons.
papers.limits: The reviewed construction has no identified LaBRADOR terminal dependency.

papers.title: Akita: A High-Performance Lattice-Based Polynomial Commitment Scheme
papers.affected_claim: Exact norm sumchecks and a separate filtered-challenge support certificate.
papers.limits: The paper expressly avoids JL projection and develops its own commitment-opening analysis.

papers.title: Jindo: Practical Lattice-Based Polynomial Commitments for Client-Side Proving
papers.affected_claim: Its own Quad/Agg/Split composition.
papers.limits: The paper explicitly evaluates the construction without LaBRADOR composition.

papers.title: LatticeBlindFold: A Lattice-Based Analogue of NovaBlindFold
papers.affected_claim: An ABDLOP-based construction.
papers.limits: The reviewed work leaves a complete decider as a further step.
